heading: The standard menus
body:
The macOS host builds the menu bar itself, so every app has the menus that a Mac user expects. The app menu has About, Hide (Command-H), Hide Others (Option-Command-H), Show All and Quit (Command-Q). Quit is the normal macOS quit, so the app cleans up once. The File menu has Close Window (Command-W). The Edit menu has Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste and Select All; they act on the field that has the focus. The View menu has Enter Full Screen, the Window menu has Minimize (Command-M), Zoom and Bring All to Front, and the Help menu has the system search.

The host adds no New, Open, Save or Print item, because a Tachyon app has no document type. Your own items cannot take a shortcut of these standard commands.

On Linux and Windows every app has a menu bar too, also when the manifest declares no items. It has File (your File items, then Close Window, Ctrl+W, and Quit, Ctrl+Q; Windows calls it Exit), Edit (Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste and Select All, which act on the focused field of the page; Redo is Ctrl+Shift+Z on Linux and Ctrl+Y on Windows), Window (Minimize and Maximize, which restores a maximized window), and View and Help when they have items. iOS and Android add no standard menus. They show your route items in their own way, described in Menu items that open a page.

Linux menus and application services are tested by building and running the real GTK 4 and WebKitGTK 6.0 host. Windows menus and application services were built with MSVC and run on Windows 11: the service starts once before the window, menu actions run, and Close Window stops the service once. That run used an SSH session, where WebView2 shows no page. Later runs on a signed-in Windows 11 ARM64 desktop showed the page inside WebView2 and made native calls from it. The menus together with that page were not yet tested there: the Edit commands inside WebView2, a page event from a menu action, and Minimize and Maximize. A Windows app is built for x64 or ARM64 (`--arch x64` or `--arch arm64`).
